articles.title: Insomniac Says Marvel's Wolverine Uses No Generative AI After Fans Spot Strange Signs in-Game
articles.summary: Insomniac Games has stepped in to confirm Marvel's Wolverine contains no generative AI after a few bizarre in-game signs raised eyebrows on social media. The hubbub surrounding the new PlayStation 5 exclusive's latest controversial moment kicked off when TikToker SmoothMango shared a video of their…
body: "Folks, that looks AI-generated," SmoothMango said. "I am trying to think of a way to describe this that is not AI generation because there's no way it's a bathroom for mutants. That looks supremely sus."

At least as it's presented here, the bathroom signs certainly seem odd. With fear surrounding AI at an all-time high, fans latched onto the clip, concerned that Insomniac had used the controversial technology to help build Marvel's Wolverine.

The glitchy bathroom signs then, of course, found their way over to X/Twitter, where user Rock Solid shared images from the video. Fans again swarmed out of fear, but Insomniac has since said its Wolverine game doesn't feature a drop of genAI.

The developer's director of community and marketing, James Stevenson, replied to the X post in question to clear the air. He said "a UV map bug" is behind the strange bathroom signs, promising that Insomniac is currently working on a fix that should address any similar instances of glitchy visuals. For those who still had question marks above their heads, Stevenson was more direct: "There are no AI-generated assets in Marvel's Wolverine."
points: Insomniac Games has stepped in to confirm Marvel's Wolverine contains no generative AI after a few bizarre in-game signs raised eyebrows on social media.

articles.title: We Ranked The 10 Best Eevee Pokémon Cards of All Time
articles.summary: We've ranked the 10 best Eevee Pokémon cards of all time, from priceless Japanese trophy promos to iconic vintage classics and modern chase cards.
body: Between a shelf overflowing with a collection of over 100 Eevee plushies and my ongoing quest to complete an ultimate Eevee Master Set binder (collecting every single variant, promo, and English card ever printed for our favorite fluffball), this Pokémon is my number one.

So with the 30th Celebration expansion release and Eeveelution chase cards dominating the market, what better time to settle this once and for all: which is the best Eevee card of all time? And I mean Eevee - pure, unevolved, Normal-type Eevee.
No disrespect to the Eeveelutions, but if we let them on this list, we all know Moonbreon would shoot to number one quicker than we can shuffle a deck.

Before we jump in, for those after 30th Celebration boosters, our best suggestion right now is to request an invite from Amazon for the ETB at least, priced much more reasonably compared to other retailers. Invites will be sent out soon!

articles.title: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan Will Destroy You at Super Smash Bros.
articles.summary: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan grew up a Nintendo kid, through and through. Growing up, the breakout star of Netflix's Never Have I Ever — and of the new movie, Best of the Best — wasn't allowed to play violent games like Call of Duty or GTA on Xbox and PlayStation.
body: She's a die-hard Smash fan, and her mastery of the game was hard-won, after years of getting stuck with the crappy, third-party controller with the chewed-up joystick. "I was really, really bad as a kid. But I kept playing. And I slowly started understanding, like, wait, you don't have to spam things. It's not random. You can actually choose moves and combos. There's a method and strategy to this. Once I learned that, I started getting way better and then started beating my cousins all the time," she explained. "And that's why I have a Kirby tattoo. That was my first tattoo."

To all the Kirby haters out there, a word of warning: "I could kick your ass without using down-B once." She adds, "I actually love to use down-B as a fake-out, because I stop it midway and do something else, and then boom, you're done."

Given that her new Netflix movie centers on a Bollywood dance club at UCLA, I assume that Ramakrishnan must be an accomplished dancer. Not quite. But she is pretty good at rhythm games. " I don't know if the people who make Just Dance know, but they were a part of my education for Best of the Best."
points: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan grew up a Nintendo kid, through and through.

articles.title: The Batman Part 2 Director Reveals New Image Seemingly Set in a Snowy Gotham Junkyard
articles.summary: The Batman Part 2 director Matt Reeves has done his part to celebrate Batman Day by sharing a new image from the movie. Another September means another Batman Day, and while we're still years away from seeing Robert Pattinson reprise his role as the Caped Crusader, that isn't stopping DC Studios…
body: If you've seen 2022's The Batman, you'll be happy to know even this early image from the movie teases a film that will feel right at home in the saga. What we see here appears to be the back of Pattinson's Bruce Wayne as he looks ahead into what seems to be a forest-y area. We can only really see his silhouette, but it's at least yet another confirmation that The Batman Part 2 will take place in and around the snow.
"Happy Batman Day to everyone from London!" Reeves said in his post.

Is there much we can confidently say this image reveals about the plot of Reeves' new movie? Well, no, but fans are still using the holiday as an opportunity to comb through every pixel of The Batman Part 2 image in hopes of deciphering any details about its plot and characters.

One rumored villain that has stuck in the years it's taken to get The Batman sequel into theaters revolves around Gotham's secret collection of evil elites, The Court of Owls. Recently leaked set photos only stoked those flames, with fans saying that, even if there aren't any owls to be found in the new set image, they're still looking for them.

articles.title: How Zach Cregger Pulled Off Resident Evil’s Most Disgusting Scenes
articles.summary: Last year, Polygon was part of a press trip that provided a behind-the-scenes look at the making of Resident Evil. I followed in the footsteps of hapless medical courier Bryan (Austin Abrams), exploring the horrors the t-virus wrought across a series of sets.
body: I have never smelled anything like the set of Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil. When I visited the massive Prague sound stage in December, the air was filled with the latex scents of enormous, grisly props combined with the sharp odor of burning metal as welders built the world of Raccoon City. A sweet aroma rose up from the fake blood that was laid on the floor so thick it stuck to the bottom of my boots.

As he tries to make his way to Raccoon City on foot, Bryan escapes into a sewer tunnel to avoid a tentacled monster. He’s drawn to a noise that sounds a bit like a prolonged belch, which turns out to be coming from a huge, naked, pale man sitting in his path. Bryan cautiously approaches, asking if the man is OK, before watching as his gut bursts and unleashes a swarm of bloody rats.
points: Last year, Polygon was part of a press trip that provided a behind-the-scenes look at the making of Resident Evil.

articles.title: The Sims 4's Next Update Will Make Your Sims Act a Lot More Naturally
articles.summary: The next Sims 4 update is just around the corner, and it looks like it'll be a game-changer for Sims' autonomy. The official EA Laundry List for the next update lets us in on some of the changes being made this week, and its quality-of-life changes have certainly been a long time coming.
body: The update is focused on both gameplay additions and bug fixes. For example, the Gallery has often failed to load search result over the past few months, but the patch will finally tackle this matter. The team has improved game stability by reviewing player crash reports and tracking down the errors causing the issues. Hopefully, these updates can prevent similar problems in the future.

The main focus of the update is Sims' autonomy, as it aims to ensure that Sim behavior is as realistic as possible. The update will make it much more common for Sims to make eye contact during conversations. Instead of washing their hands in the kitchen sink after using the bathroom, Sims will finally use the sink closest to the toilet.

Speaking of going to the bathroom, Sims will walk faster when their Bladder Need is particularly low. As for those with a low Energy Need, they will actually sleep through the night rather than wake up to do random activities. Those may seem like small updates individually, but together they should give Sims much more realistic behaviors.
points: The next Sims 4 update is just around the corner, and it looks like it'll be a game-changer for Sims' autonomy.

articles.title: 'The largest theft of labor in human history:' Court docs reveal Microsoft exec predicted AI 'doom loops' could hollow out the internet
articles.summary: In Dec. 2023, The New York Times filed one of the biggest copyright lawsuits in recent memory against OpenAI and Microsoft, alleging that its AI models heisted ludicrous amounts of journalistic work from the Times.
body: Perhaps the most shocking sentiments are from Microsoft's director of applied science, Brent Hecht, who wrote in an internal presentation that Copilot's answer engine would "hurt the performance of our models and the entire web at the same time."

Internal data from Microsoft suggests that the engine caused click-through rates for The New York Times search results to drop at rates between 87% to 93% compared to standard Bing searches. For Ziff Davis domains—the company that owns Eurogamer and IGN—click-through rates dropped between 51% and 94%.

The filing also reveals that when a researcher for OpenAI, Nick Ryder, told OpenAI president Greg Brockman about "a hack to get around nytimes paywall" to help scrape its writing, Brockman replied "ah nice." OpenAI internal documents see Brockman writing that LLMs are "very good at any news task."

articles.title: Star Wars Zero Company Unofficially Gets A Real Endgame
articles.summary: Star Wars Zero Company is a fantastic strategy game, but it lacks a real endgame. Once you roll credits, you're simply encouraged to start a new save where you have some additional customization options and can recruit clone troopers from the start.
body: Cafiso's Aftermath DLC mod, which launched earlier in September but gained traction online this week, adds 1,000 more rotations (in-game days) to the strategy game. Once PC players roll credits, they can keep completing operations and missions, level up their characters, and earn more gear.

The mod doesn't simply increase the number of rotations at players' disposal, though. It also offers new enemy encounters and layers of progression to fill that added time. It added boss fights for Boba Fett, Palpatine, Gar Saxon, Rook Kast, Clone Commander, Purge Trooper, and Imperial Jet Trooper Commander, and turned Rex, Anakin, Cody, Baker, and Captain Crovo into recruitable characters. The player's Den Level cap has been raised to 15, while character bonds go up to +12 and focus trees now have 11 tiers.

On top of that, players can toggle an "Aftermath Threat" system that slightly increases enemies' health, shields, and damage after each encounter, and an "Aftermath Fatigue" system that debuffs operators if they are repeatedly used on back-to-back missions. It's quite impressive for an unofficial fan-made mod and is much more entertaining than simply starting a new playthrough.
points: Star Wars Zero Company is a fantastic strategy game, but it lacks a real endgame.

articles.title: I played the adventure game so scandalous that it was physically destroyed by UK customs
articles.summary: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex.
body: Weird Weekend is our regular Saturday column where we celebrate PC gaming oddities: peculiar games, strange bits of trivia, forgotten history. Pop back every weekend to find out what Jeremy, Josh, Rick and Ted have become obsessed with this time, whether it's the canon height of Thief's Garrett or that time someone in the Vatican pirated Football Manager.

Videogames have been banned and censored for all manner of reasons, and at least one game was so notoriously terrible that it was buried in the desert. But I've never heard of a game being so repellent that it was physically destroyed before. I've played some rotten games in my time, but I've never felt a desire to eradicate any of them from existence.

Yet this is exactly what happened to Sex Vixens from Space, a lewd graphic adventure developed by Free Spirit Software and released in 1988. Initially launched in the US, Sex Vixens from Space was meant to arrive in the UK the following year. But it never did—at least, not officially, because the shipment was intercepted and destroyed by UK Customs.

articles.title: It rules that a 27-year-old RPG, one of the greatest of all time, is still getting patches
articles.summary: A lamentable fact of our hobby is this: time marches on. Because our games have to be rendered in real-time by whatever tech we load them onto, they inevitably end up harder to run as the years wear on, and the gap grows between the tech we have and the tech the games were designed to run on.
body: You can't expect devs to maintain games in perpetuity. Unless, I guess, they happen to be the stewards of the Baldur's Gate and Planescape: Torment Enhanced Editions, which are still getting patches almost three decades after the original games released. Most recently (September 15), Planescape got a beta update to its, uh, beta update: a release candidate for an upcoming patch that will bring the game in line with the 2.7 patches some of Beamdog's other Enhanced Edition games already have.

As with those other games, the new Planescape beta (itself an addition to a previous beta from August) makes Steam Cloud saves work how they ought to: toggleable through the Steam client itself rather than via in-game options. GOG cloud saves now actually work, too and—this is probably the biggest thing—Planescape now has a UI scaling option in its settings. Leave it off and the game will keep its UI at god's own resolution, 1024x768, but if you flick it on it will adapt to better fit modern monitors. Like yours!

articles.title: HoYoverse's Nodusfall might look like Elden Ring, but there's a promising dark fantasy action game here that took me by surprise
articles.summary: Nodusfall, aesthetically at least, is about as far from a typical HoYoverse game as you can get. Gone are the bright colours, cute creatures, and bountiful anime women.
body: I'll admit to being a little worried at the beginning of my preview after learning it would consist of two boss battles fought in groups of four. After all, the majority of my co-op experience comes from RuneScape, a 25-year-old MMORPG primarily played with a mouse, and nobody wants to let their team down.

But first came the character selection. There were four options available in my demo: two focused around melee combat, two ranged. Both combat styles offered one character with healing-focused abilities which I immediately discounted - too much responsibility. The archer with a mechanical arm though? Inflicting heavy damage from a distance while taking care of any nasty surprises was definitely something I could do. Decision made, it was time to discover how my chosen role would actually play out in battle.
points: Nodusfall, aesthetically at least, is about as far from a typical HoYoverse game as you can get.

articles.title: This unofficial engine patch for Thief: The Dark Project adds a huge new feature that won't be in Nightdive's upcoming remaster
articles.summary: Thief: The Dark Project is one of my favourite games of all time, so naturally I am very excited for Nightdive Studios' upcoming remaster. But it's worth remembering that the community has done an excellent job supporting the game up until this point.
body: And if you thought an official remaster might put such efforts to an end, think again. Not to be outdone by Nightdive, NewDark's creator just released a new version of the overhaul which adds a radical new feature to Thief—dynamic shadows.

Yep, NewDark 1.29 introduces hardware transform & lighting to the Dark Engine, opening the door to GPU-driven effects in Thief's gothic steampunk world. Chief among these is shadows that are dynamically cast by moving objects—guards, doors, even master thief Garrett himself.

The update's effects were shown off in a YouTube video by Thief fan Bentraxx. What's particularly interesting about the dynamic shadows is not simply how they look, but the mechanical implications they have. For example, opening a door between a dark corridor and a well-lit room will flood the former with light, while opened doors create shadows behind them, meaning Garrett can now use doors to create hiding spaces.
points: Thief: The Dark Project is one of my favourite games of all time, so naturally I am very excited for Nightdive Studios' upcoming remaster.

articles.title: Indie Dev Says “AI” Voice In His Game Was Actually His Wife
articles.summary: Someone playing Refractive Entertainment's recently released action-RPG Luminary for less than an hour accused the team of using AI for the game's only voiced character. The player said the voice "killed it" for them. There was just one problem: It wasn't AI.
body: Refractive Entertainment launched Luminary into Steam Early Access on August 11. It's a resource-gathering action-adventure sandbox with an art style that's giving Fable meets Immortals Fenyx Rising. It's cute-looking and well-received, with a "Mostly Positive" rating out of almost 350 Steam reviews. But for an indie developer who says his game's success lives and dies by its Steam review score, one particular negative review caught the creative director's attention.

On September 10, user NyteKnyte posted a short Steam review after only 0.4 hours with the game to say that Luminary looked good but "the awful AI-generated voice killed it" for them. "Feels off, like an AI game," NyteKnyte said in their review. "Hopefully its temporary and gets better, but [the AI voice] killed it for me."
Not long after this review hit the game's Steam page, Refractive Entertainment responded, saying that the “awful AI-generated voice” that NyteKnyte decried was actually the creative director's wife.

videos.title: The Resident Evil Movie Understands Video Games Are Ridiculous, and That's Why It's Great
videos.summary: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie understands that video games are ridiculous, and that's why it's great.
body: Video games are ridiculous. The Resident Evil series is a perfect example. One moment you’re running in terror from a comically oversized, trench-coated tank of a man in a tiny hat; the next, you’re messing around with electronic chess pieces to open a door. These are completely alien situations that, somehow, these games compel us to navigate with rational thought. This is what Zach Cregger understands so well about Capcom’s genre-defining series. His Resident Evil movie knows this is ridiculous, so it lets its lead, Brian, progress through a 90-minute rollercoaster just as we would with a controller in our hands. It’s a fantastic translation of the sensation of playing a survival horror game, never forgetting to include every piece of glorious nonsense that comes with it.
points: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie understands that video games are ridiculous, and that's why it's great.

In Kingmakers, go back in time to a war-torn medieval era with a vast arsenal of modern weapons, change the course of history, and save the future in this epic action/strategy sandbox.
Build your kingdom, grab a gun, and lead an army of thousands into massive, real-time simulated battles — solo or in co-op for up to four players.
